boundaries: No actual App automation by this subagent; DOM events run in jsdom. Root supplies A-layer focus/terminal/read-error visibility.
Ordinary external writer is a direct independent filesystem writer; CLI writer is a separate Electron-as-Node process. No actual third-party GUI writer in I; root tests TextEdit in A.

Rich Markdown is the real production parser/Worker/widgets. Only Worker communication is adapted to node:worker_threads; code syntax worker is isolated because fixtures have headings/emphasis, no code fences.
File panel hide/remount in I is component/store lifecycle. No real PTY here and no inference that disk change means a CLI task finished. Root supplies actual terminal switch/PID evidence.
Native broker comes from r5; TypeScript sources match frozen r6 snapshot. This does not claim r5 App contains DEV047 or later product changes.
No source-file save calls or checkpoint calls in clean scenarios. Conflict scenario may schedule recovery checkpoint but no source-file save.

case.expected: Clean Markdown external changes refresh exact source and rich document via native watch, reactivation and explicit refresh for CLI and ordinary writers; real read errors remain clear and recover; no old-content writeback or CLI approval. Only later real local dirty plus differing disk enters ordinary conflict.
matrix: separate CLI process × native watch/reactivation/explicit refresh
case.eachSuccess: Two external revisions; real Worker heading/strong DOM and source EditorView match exact latest bytes. source→document toggles remain clean, disk hash/mtime/ctime/inode unchanged by App, no save/checkpoint calls.
case.error: Actual rename away produces [MISSING] native error while retaining previous source; restore same file + new bytes clears error and renders newest heading.
case.dirtyBoundary: Actual EditorView transaction after clean synchronization keeps local text and exposes separately-read disk conflict when a further CLI change differs.
